findings.problem: No page could be opened (Wikipedia, Wisconsin Historical Society, HISTORY, UPI and others failed or were refused), so every passage is search-summary text, and many outlets were filed by inference. 14 medium-risk historical claims rest on one sure outlet group and are REQUIRES REVIEW.
findings.recommendation: Read in full: the Wisconsin Historical Society's Gein entries, the 1957 Wisconsin State Journal coverage, UPI's 1984 obituary and Judge Gollmar's 1981 book; record full_text access.

findings.problem: Legal record stated exactly: found to have committed first-degree murder of Bernice Worden and legally insane (1968), committed, never imprisoned; admitted the Hogan killing (per investigators) but never charged or tried; never charged over Henry's death, which the film calls speculation.

Nothing found in the house is described beyond grave robbing and kept remains; no remains, body or weapon is drawn; victims appear only as silhouette cards; named missing people once checked against him are not named.
findings.recommendation: Keep the same restraint in comments and Shorts.

findings.problem: Gate G9 flags the word 'Monster' in the title. It is the Netflix series' name (Monster: The Ed Gein Story), not our characterisation; the description gives the legal record directly.
findings.recommendation: Keep, or use the alternative 'Ed Gein: Myth vs Fact, From the Record'.

findings.problem: 'Gein' is respelled 'Geen' (the usual pronunciation); Schley, Waupun, Waushara and Gollmar are respelled and not verified by ear.
